author: hoeschec
text:
So...I am going to spend some time going back through some of Salivan's trades. I will be referencing his journal entries if you are interested, you can follow along or add your input. The dissection room for IF's trades is really interesting, but IF doesn't provide much detail on his trades, so it leaves more questions than answers-at least for me (...BTW...I have nothing but respect for IF

).

I have found three trades that Salivan has posted in his journal (although I'm sure there are more) that I want to investigate. We are coming up on a new year and I am seriously motivated to achieve a break through in my trading.

To date, I have not been able to put all the pieces together...and while I think there are multiple strategies that can be successful under the umbrella of RTM, I have come to be most interested in Salivan's trades. He posts amazing trades with very little DD and explains himself in a way that I find extremely useful and logical (his top down analysis is a rare find). I like Salivan's approach of the market and I want to learn more about how he finds his trade opportunities and why he takes trades where he does.

I need to be focused and avoid distractions...there are many ways to apply the wonderful knowledge that RTM offers, and it's time for me to start focusing on consistency. Just like Mertch specializes in trading the QM and LP focused on the 'sweet FTR'.... I need to start molding my own strategy based on how my brain best processes all of this information. I don't know where I will end up, but I am starting with Salivan's trades.

The three trades I am gong to start with can be found on the following posts in "Art of War" Journal:

Post # 471www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum...art-of-war?start=450

Post # 548www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum...art-of-war?start=525

Post # 552 www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum...art-of-war?start=550

In particular, I need to research the following:

1. How to incorporate scale in determining which areas will bounce price 2. Answering the question "where is price coming from" and "where is price going" 3. Understanding which FO's matter the most - specifically, what is the significance of a FO occurring in to another FL? 4. Practice finding targets for all engulfs - regardless of the scale 5. Understanding the difference between origins and true supply/demand 6. Difference between FO and EG as it relates to scale 7. Learning more about the deep RT and understanding why it happens 8. Learning to think like an IT 9. Developing a consistent approach for top down analysis and being disciplined to complete a top down analysis before every trade 10. Focus, focus, focus on specific setups that are rooted in sound theory (everything should be explainable in terms of order flow) 11. Not all tricks are created equal...some are more important than others. Why?

Salivan keeps telling me to focus on the price reading article on marketpedia. I have to be honest...I always resist that specific advice from him because I have read that article many times and found it to be unhelpful and vague. That said, I need to set aside my opinions of this article and trust that there is something critical to find within those words. Blind stubbornness is often a product of one's ignorance.. I must rid myself of this bad habit. I will read the article every day until I understand what it is talking about. I need to set aside some of my assumptions and practice opening my mind to the bigger concepts at play. It is time to read between the lines and apply it to Salivan's top down analysis.

If anyone is interested in going down this path with me, please feel free to post your opinions here

The price reading article is found here:

www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/education/markepedia

The price reading article can be separated in three main parts:

1. Past 2. Approach 3. Reaction

Salivan asks similar questions on his charts:

1. Where is price coming from? (PAST) 2. Where it is now? (PRESENT) 3. Where must price go? (FUTURE...ALSO DEPENDENT ON PAST DP's) 4. How is price approaching? (APPROACH) 5. How is price behaving now? (APPROACH & REACTION)

author: hoeschec
text:
"Where is price coming from" is question that is hard for me to comprehend because I it confusing...lack of specific context (it is a general question that could have multiple answers....). Because of this confusion, I haven't considered the importance of this question as it relates to scale. I still don't know for sure, but by going back through Salivan's trades I notice he tends to answer this question in one of two ways...this may be the hint I need to provide more clarity.

He always answers this question one of two ways:

1. Price is coming from a Reached target [/u] 2. Price is coming from an Unreached target[/u]

Why is knowing whether price has hit its target important (isn't it the EG of the target that matters most)? And which target are we supposed to use?... there are many targets on many scales.

How is knowing whether price is coming from a HTF 'reached target' important to our trading?

How is knowing whether price is coming from a HTF 'reached target' important to the issue of scale

There are two main points of confusion that I must focus on:

First, I don't understand how to apply the concept of the reached/unreached target from a theoretical perspective. I don't understand what specific implications it has on my trading.

Second, I am still somewhat confused on how to properly draw the targets in different scales. Sometimes the targets jump out at me and other times they are elusive and seem subjective.

...I have theoretical and practical confusion on this topic...the worst combo

Perhaps the better question to ask is: What's the difference between trading in a scenario where price is coming from a reached target versus a scenario where price is coming from an unreached target?

author: hoeschec
text:
(continued from post # 1412)

When faced with theoretical and practical confusion on a topic I think it is more useful to start with the theory. Once the theory is understood the practical may work itself out.

Let's approach it this way: we can assume the issue of reached vs unreached target is important. So..I will ask this question (technically two questions):

Why does price act differently when coming from a reached vs. unreached target and as a follow up question, how does it act differently?

- Are there FL's that are 'in play' in situations where price is coming from a reached target that otherwise would not be 'in play' if price was coming from a reached target

- We are always trying to understand which extreme level price will FO to after an engulf so we can get in the trade without getting stopped out...Does this 'extreme' level change depending on whether price is coming from a reached target vs. an unreached target? If so, why is this the case (in terms of OF)?

- Are there specific levels that become irrelevant (with regard to FOF) once a target has been met? Are there specific levels that become relevant (with regard to OF) once a target has been met?

I wonder if it has something to do with anticipating a FO..if price is coming from an unreached target we should be prepared for a FO to the extreme set of orders in the zone...we would expect tricks to get played to load the IT's with liquidity to reach the target. If price is coming from a reached target, maybe we identify the same break of a FL as an engulf instead of a FO. Does the labeling of a FO/EG depend (in part) on whether price is coming from a reached vs. unreached target?

If so, this may be how Salivan knows which 'trick' levels to choose.... He chooses previous FO's that occurred prior to price hitting its target. Those same zones may not react the same way if they were formed after price already reached its target. It would explain why some FO areas bounce price and others do not...
